key_insight: A FEM-validated graph neural network can deliver real-time, sub-millimetre prediction of soft tactile deformation using only a small set of physical validations plus synthetic FEM data.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast, accurate virtual prototyping of planar soft tactile sensors and contact localization without expensive repeated physical testing or minute-scale simulation.
method: Use 82 camera-tracked real contact cases to tune and validate an ANSYS FEM model.
Generate 768 synthetic contact scenarios from the validated FEM for GNN training.
Deploy the trained GNN for forward and inverse deformation prediction in a real-time visualization pipeline.
evidence_signal: The validated FEM achieved under 0.5 mm error in over 90% of validation cases, and the GNN reached 0.32 mm mean absolute error with millisecond-scale inference on the 2D tactile structure.
watch_item: The demonstrated sim-to-real transfer is strongest for the tested planar setting, so performance may not directly generalize to more complex geometries or loading conditions without revalidation.
paper_title: FEM-Validated Real-Time Modelling of Soft Tactile Deformation
